Two more runs: 145 places, then 4 that stood at the very end of a text and were skipped by a fault in the script's own guard, found by scanning the built pages. In all 214 places in the running text of 17 lessons, and 12 titles. notes.6: Decision 6, the engine: done and tested. Before scripts/person_forms.py was touched the split was written (data/person_forms_split.json: last digit of the entry number, odd = open 1,065 verbs, even = sealed 1,059; the hash of the engine file as it then was; what Stage 2 had already shown; 39 sealed verbs found in the record of the working session as displayed before, to be reported apart). On the open half the engine as reviewed gave 746 of 995 (75.0%); by rule ti- to ra- 464 of 470, the h- variant 86 of 87, tu- to ru- 157 of 166, tiʔ- to raʔ- 25 of 29, the three misread rules 14 of 243. A mechanical search of the open half found no rule for the tii- verbs (best 74.5%) nor for tih- with another headword (2 verbs): they get no form. Because tu- and tiʔ- do not reach 97% by themselves on the open half, two configurations were written down before the opening (data/person_forms_plan.json), with the rule for which ships: "narrow", the repair as the paper lists it, and "strict", only rules at 97% on the open half. Repair applied: the three rules out; no invented tiku- first person; no present or future for "I" and "you"; rules in a table with their open-half figures; --validate-appendix fails on any mismatch (26 passed, 0 failed, 2 declined). The sealed half was opened once (scripts/engines_review/person_forms_repair.py --sealed; it refuses a second run): narrow gives a form for 816 of 1,059 verbs and 794 start as form 4 starts, 97.3%, bar 97% reached (773 of 784 without the 39 displayed verbs); strict 562 of 572, 98.3%. Narrow ships by the rule of the plan. Weak point reported, not changed: tiʔ- to raʔ- agreed for 12 of 19 sealed verbs. Record: reports/engines_review/person_forms_repair.md. Still to do under this decision, with decision 8: the sentence builder passes the entry and labels every derived form.
notes.8: Decision 8 done, and with it the builder part of decision 6. scripts/sentence_templates.py and scripts/template_slot_fillers.py are rebuilt around printed rows. A pattern starts from a sentence the Blue Book prints (13 frames for the ten patterns, each named by the number and the text of its row of blue_book_attestations); a word may be swapped only for another printed word, given by its row; no Pawnee word is typed in either file. The result says "printed in the Blue Book, lesson N" only when it is, accents included, a form of the table; otherwise "put together here; not printed". "The stick is red" takes the quality as a phrase the book lists, or in the dictionary's spelling the entry's printed form 2 (rakis tipahaaʔat, not ti + the stem). Dictionary verbs are a separate part in Parks's spelling, never mixed into a Blue Book sentence: chosen by entry id (/api/verbs returns it; "I" and "you" only where a form 1 is printed), their forms shown as printed or as "derived; not checked against a printed form" (/api/verb-forms), and sentences in the dictionary's spelling made by /api/dictionary-sentence with Parks's question words by entry. The three non-words are gone with the typed lists.
